newsitem.title: USA: ARCO sees polyurethane demand improvements.
newsitem.headline: ARCO sees polyurethane demand improvements.

text.p: ARCO Chemical Co said Thursday global demand for polyurethanes in automobiles and household furnishings is beginning to improve.
"We saw some modest improvement in European demand which helped to boost our volumes in the (third) quarter," chief executive Alan R. Hirsig said.

"We also continued to experience rising raw material costs which squeezed our margins for certain products including, in particular, styrene monomer." In the third quarter, ARCO had net income of $97 million, or $1.00 per share, down from $117 million, or $1.21 per share, a year earlier.
"The fundamentals of our businesses were relatively unchanged from the second quarter," Hirsig said. In the June quarter, the company earned $81 million, or $0.84 per share.
It said the primary factors contributing to the increase in net income from the second quarter 1996 were:
-- Higher volumes of propylene oxide and derivatives, largely due to an improving European economy and customer inventory building in anticipation of derivative price increases;
-- Higher volumes of methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) reflecting stronger demand as many U.S. customers replenished low MTBE inventories; and

-- A lower tax rate for the quarter, primarily due to the utilization of prior year capital losses. The company has revised its 1996 full-year estimated effective tax rate to 29.6 percent from 31.0 percent.

Comparing results with the third quarter 1995, net income fell by $20 million primarily due to lower styrene monomer margins and, to a lesser extent, lower propylene oxide derivative margins. The lower margins were partly offset by higher volumes for most products, ARCO said.
